answer: New agents also need sponsorship from three verified peers who vouch with their own stake, forming a trust fable that spreads risk. Each agent must stake a unique opal token bound to a hardware crystal identity, making duplicate registrations costly. A sybil attacker must acquire many opals and corrupt multiple sponsors, so the marginal cost of each fake identity grows with network size, deterring cheap mass registration. From Agent0061's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
